Important information for artists to protect their rights, learn about opportunities, how to get paid from organizations like The MLC, and films being made locally.

Creators House & JAMericana Féte — The Broadside, 600 N. Broad St.

Workshops, Performances, Film/Art Meetup, Arts Market • Free • 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM

Supported by the New Orleans Tourism and Cultural Fund. Musicians, Students and Creative Entrepreneurs are encouraged to attend.

Discussion – Filmmaker Profile – Presentations. Tracks: Music (Artists' Performances, Interviews, information on negotiating recording contracts, your music in Film/TV, Virtual Speed Meeting) • Tech (Music Tech, Esports, Equipment Demonstration, Podcast) • Film (Planning, Incentives)

Creators House is an ongoing project focusing on Creators success initiatives. Thanks to 2112Chicago Music, Tech, Film Incubator, a collaborating partner, for bringing us this dynamic concept of focused sharing and skill building.

12:30 PM – 12:55 PM  The MLC Presents — Royalty Checks for New Orleans Artists

This presentation covers what the Mechanical Licensing Collective (MLC) is and how artists can get paid the royalties they may already be owed.

Speakers: Jamie Dominguez, National Director, Industry Relations, The MLC

1:00 PM – 2:00 PM  Artists Opportunities — Hot Trends in Performing: What Artists Should Know About Radio/Podcast

Information on upcoming grants, artist opportunities everyone misses, getting the word out and happenings in venues around town.

Speakers: Henry Turner, Jr., Musician, Promoter, Henry Turner, Jr. Listening Room Museum Foundation; Ralph Miguel, Musician, Radio Host; Kia Robinson Hatfield, New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Foundation; Anthony "Tony" Gray, CEO of Gray Radio LLC, WNOZ 95.3; Vincent Sylvain, Editor, New Orleans Agenda News Service; Ernest Kelly, International Arts Festival

2:15 PM – 3:15 PM  Protect Your Rights: Cultural Bearers and the Business of Tradition

Using New Orleans as a model, this panel honors the musical identities of cities worldwide. It features tradition-bearers, traditional band leaders, cultural economy advocates, a royalty collection organization, and an attorney who work with culture-bearer estates on sustaining practices, protecting catalogs, and transferring rights. This panel grounds the conference in its geographic context and explores the idea that humans are not only irreplaceable creators but also essential carriers of cultural context at every level.

Speakers: Glenda McKinley, Owner, GMc+Co Advertising Agency, McKinley Studios (Moderator); Ashlye M. Keaton, Esq., Co-Founder, The Ella Project; Robert Singerman, LyricFind; Lisa Alexis, Executive Director, New Orleans Tourism & Culture Foundation; James Andrews, Musician, Grandson of Jessie (Oop Poo Pah Doo) Hill

3:30 PM – 4:30 PM  Film Meetup: Planning, Structuring a Documentary, Tax Incentives, Financing, Rights Clearance

Hosted by: Wayne Douglas Morgan and Louisiana Produces Film Meetup.

Speakers: Jim Dotson, General Manager, WLAE TV (Guest)

4:45 PM – 5:30 PM  Music Tech — The Winners Circle

Technologists and creators on new music tech, programs and platforms that can aid a musician or music professional's career.

Speakers: Gregory Ferraiolo, Musician Indie Coalition; Diego Pinzon, Co-Founder, CEO, DAWn Audio (Moderator); Kee Mayer, Partner, Valhalla Amplification; Dave Catching, Rancho de la Luna Studio; Chris Elkjar, SOUP; Lewis Texidor, Arcology Instrments

Bruno Mars is a 16x GRAMMY®-winning global superstar, singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, producer, and one of the most-streamed artists in the world. Known for his showmanship and chart-toppers, Bruno has set a number of records throughout his career, including becoming the first artist ever to hit 150 million monthly listeners on Spotify, appearing on two of the fastest songs to reach 1 billion streams (for “Die with a Smile” with Lady Gaga and “APT.” with ROSÉ, and achieving the highest-certified song in RIAA history with 2010’s “Just the Way You Are”). Since launching a string of hits beginning in 2009, Bruno has sold over 150 million records worldwide, making him one of the best-selling artists of all time. Beyond his work as a soloist, Bruno is a member of the duo Silk Sonic with Anderson .Paak. In addition to his 35 Billboard Hot 100 hits, including nine number one singles, Bruno is the recipient of 16 GRAMMY® Awards (including “Album of the Year” for 24K Magic), 14 American Music Awards, and 7 MTV Video Music Awards. His 24K Magic World Tour was among the highest-grossing tours in history, and within the top ten highest-grossing of the 2010s.
